pairs.question: An Deus omnipotens cuius sub nutu reguntur omnia, non valeat post mortem reddere vitam, aut aliquid rerum Dominum non posse videtur?
pairs.answer: Cum sint cuncta Dei, reddit magis omnia tellus, iussa revocabit quidquid contexerat olim.
pairs.derivation: Authorial rhetorical question (can the omnipotent God not restore life after death, is anything beyond the Lord's power?). The reply opens with a non-answering preamble that is itself a further rhetorical question (lines 110-115: 'si potuit tenebris... cur non ex aliquo possit conpingere notam... similemque suae iubeat resurgere formam?'), so the answer's start is advanced past it to the operative affirming declarative at lines 116-117, which directly answers the question: since all things are God's, the earth all the more restores them, recalling whatever it had buried. Window ends there before the poem turns to the seed/star analogies.
